nodes.name: Ni/NiO@HGPxOy impregnation-reduction
nodes.procedure: An impregnation-reduction method was used to prepare Ni/NiO@HGPxOy catalysts. Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and HGPxOy were dispersed in ethanol. Ni was loaded at 3±0.2 wt%, measured by inductively coupled plasma (ICP). The impregnated material was appropriately hydrolysed to crystallise the precursors by decomposing the nickel precursor species in a tube furnace at 310 °C under a He atmosphere (total flow of 100 sccm). Furthermore, considering the fact that this decomposition condition might not be sufficient to obtain complete Ni/NiO core–shell hybrids, a second step of calcination was carried out at 400 °C in a flow of 25% H2 mixed with He (total flow of 100 sccm) for further reduction to obtain Ni/NiO@HGPxOy. Finally, the sample was cooled down to room temperature under He, and the products were removed from the corundum tube.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiO@HGPxOy shows particle size range of 2.9 nm with average size 5.2 nm; Ni/NiO@HG shows 3-15 nm range with average 7.6 nm. Nanoparticles uniformly dispersed on wrinkled graphene layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The particle sizes were estimated from the TEM images... The particle size range of Ni/NiO@HGPxOy particles was 2·9 nm, with an average size of 5.2 nm, whereas that of Ni/NiO@HG was 3-15 nm (average size: 7.6 : nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-STEM shows marked lattice fringes corresponding to Ni(111) and NiO(111) crystal planes for Ni/NiO@HGPxOy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-STEM imaging results for Ni/NiO@HGPxOy are shown in Fig. 2c and d, and the marked lattice fringes correspond to the Ni(111) and NiO(111) crystal planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDX mapping shows well-dispersed Ni/NiO core-shell structures with thin oxide layers of about 1.5 nm and homogeneous distribution of C, N, O, and Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM imaging and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping results for Ni/NiO@HGPxOy are shown in Fig. 2e, indicating the well-dispersed Ni/NiO core–shell structures with thin oxide layers of about 1.5 nm and a homogeneous distribution of C, N, O, and Ni in the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks at 44.5° and 43.3° corresponding to Ni(111) and NiO(200) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the catalysts (Fig. S3†), the diffraction peaks at 44.5° and 43.3° correspond to the (111) plane of Ni (JCPDS no. 04-0850) and the (200) plane of NiO (JCPDS no. 47-1049).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiO@HGPxOy shows P 2p peaks at 132.2 eV (oxidized P) and 133.6 eV (C6H5OPO); Ni 2p peaks at 852.7 eV (2p3/2 metallic Ni), 869.8 eV (2p1/2 metallic Ni), 855.8 eV (2p3/2 Ni2+), 873.5 eV (2p1/2 Ni2+). Ni peaks shifted to higher binding energies compared to Ni/NiO@HG due to HGPxOy interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The P 2p XPS spectrum is shown in Fig. 3b. The lowest binding energy peak was at 132.2 eV, which represented oxidized P compounds... and the peak around 133.6 eV was assigned to (C6H5O)3PO... The Ni 2p peaks at around 852.7 (2p3/2) and 869.8 eV (2p1/2) indicate the presence of metallic Ni. Moreover, the Ni 2p3/2 peak around 855.8 eV and the Ni 2p1/2 peak around 873.5 eV indicate that Ni2+ is formed... Compared with those of Ni/NiO@HG, the Ni 2p peaks of Ni/NiO@HGPxOy were shifted to higher binding energies...

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl = 0.00908 mF cm^-2 for Ni/NiO@HGPxOy (vs 0.00408 mF cm^-2 for Ni/NiO@HG), corresponding to 1.0×10^-3 mol g^-1 active sites (vs 0.47×10^-3 mol g^-1).
